We came here for my husband’s 60th birthday. You can tell from the photos that the hotel is dated, so that was not a surprise to us. When I read the reviews and saw a 4.6-star rating, I was expecting a nice hotel, but it is a little odd. Driving up to the hotel, you're not even sure it's the entrance.

We arrived, and when we got to our room, it smelled a little like smoke as well as animals. I knew they accepted dogs, but when I called beforehand, I was assured they were kept in a separate section of the hotel. Of course, later I saw a large dog in the lobby. Again, I knew they accepted dogs, so it really wasn't a problem.

We went into the quaint town of Helen and never heard from anyone at the hotel, so we went to the small office desk in the lobby and asked about the smells. They moved us to the room next door. The room was comfortable, large, had a sitting area, and the shower was nice. 

The next morning, I took a walk around the grounds to check out the tennis court. I need to attach a picture because it was a little scary and definitely not usable. They should not advertise that they have a tennis court. As I called beforehand to make sure they had a tennis court and pickleball. 

The next day, we headed into Helen again and wanted to return to the hotel for just an hour or so before heading back out, but we couldn't find a parking space. We had to head down a steep hill where there were some spaces, then drove back up the hill to see if one had opened up. They have a large section of about five valet spaces. A woman from the hotel drove by on a golf cart, and my husband asked if we could park in one of the spaces for an hour. She said they were reserved for those coming for dinner. My husband sarcastically replied, "Not for those staying here for four nights?" She was a nice lady, but that seemed odd. She removed one of the cones, and we parked in one of the five open spaces. The place was very slow and seasonal.

The funny thing is that after being there for two nights, and with only a few guests around, she even asked, "Well, are you staying here at the hotel?" She didn't remember us, and we had spoken with her three times. I promise you, we are easy people. 

We understand that nothing is going to be perfect, and we can accept that. But not remembering us after several interactions felt a little disconcerting when you're hoping for a special experience.

Meanwhile, it is now the next day, and I'm sitting in the lobby. No one has come to talk to me about the tennis court. We mentioned the room smell, we mentioned the tennis court, and we had to follow up ourselves by the end of the day. It's just a little disappointing when you're looking forward to a special getaway and feel like your concerns are not being addressed.

That said, we did enjoy the warm chocolate chip cookies that were available in the evenings. They were a nice touch. And I should mention our first night we had dinner at the hotel and it was good. The onion rings were our favorite.

Okay, one last experience. My husband is a golfer and I am not - I am a beginner. We decided for our last day we would play golf in the afternoon even if it’s just to hit on the practice range. I told my husband I do not want to bother other golfers. We go to the pro shop and my husband asks if there is a time and mentions I am a beginner and he said they were truly filled up and that is fine as we did not set an appt but when my husband mentions we’d like to practice a little on the range and you can see no one is out there at this time, he replies we don’t have any practice balls as he looks around - but you are more than welcome to take the golf cart and pick up some balls yourselves. We proceed to do this and when we head down there we practice a little and another couple come down as well and they say to us, wow we’ve never had this before, picking up your own practice balls. 

Anyways, wanted to mention our last experience. It is a shame, we will never come back to Valhalla Resort again.

Unfortunately, this experience completely changed my perception of the RIU brand. Because of how we were treated, I will never return to this resort, nor will I book another RIU property anywhere in the world.

Unsafe and Unsanitary. We arrived late after a baseball game and initially had a positive impression because check-in went smoothly. Unfortunately, everything after that was unbelievable.

The first room we were assigned appeared to be a storage room. It was filled with extra furniture, lamp shades, and even a ladder. We returned to the front desk, and the employee apologized and gave us another room.

The second room had clearly been left unsecured, with the lock pushed between the wall and the door as if it had been propped open. The room smelled strongly of cigarette smoke, and there were cigarette butts sitting on the table. It looked as though someone had been in the room smoking.

After another apology, we were assigned a third room. This one smelled like the pool, had towels scattered all over the bathroom floor, and the beds had clearly been slept in. It was obvious the room had not been cleaned or prepared for a new guest.

The front desk employee expressed frustration because her computer showed the room as clean and available, so she assigned us a fourth room. At this point, we were still trying to be patient and understanding.

When we opened the door to the fourth room, there was literally a man asleep in the bed, snoring, with his clothes laid out on a chair. I was completely mortified.

At that point, I immediately requested a refund and left. To the employee’s credit, she was kind, apologetic, and willing to help process the refund. My frustration is not with her personally. However, I have never experienced anything like this at any hotel. Being assigned four unusable rooms in a row including one that was already occupied is a serious failure in housekeeping, room management, and guest safety. I cannot recommend staying here.
